intro: Pause for a moment: you are standing at Göbekli Tepe, a sanctuary in Şanlıurfa province dating to 9600 BC. This is the world's oldest known temple complex, and its T-shaped pillars rewrote history.
history: Who built it? Not farmers, but hunter-gatherers, millennia before agriculture. Its discovery reversed an old assumption: that settlement came first, and monumental religion only afterwards.
structure-1: You are now looking at Enclosures A–D, one of the oldest monumental structures known and the earliest dated of the circles. Look at the two pillars at its centre: they have arms, hands and a belt. These stones are human in form, and they face one another.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the T-shaped pillars and their animal reliefs, and take note of the protective canopy.
facts: Did you know? Göbekli Tepe predates Stonehenge by about 6,000 years and the pyramids of Giza by 7,000. Its builders were hunter-gatherers, not farmers, which reversed the assumption that people settle down first and build temples afterwards. The T-shaped pillars carry carved foxes, snakes, scorpions and cranes, and the heaviest weighs about sixteen tonnes.
outro: Our tour of Göbekli Tepe ends here. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These pillars have waited a very long time; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
